messages:
support-ryan: Heads-up: multiple customers reporting increased 502s and timeouts hitting hosted inference in us-west-2 (around 11:40 PDT). Customers see spikes in retries and auth errors in the gateway logs. Escalating.
sre-alex: Looking at metrics now — 5xx rate from gw-usw2-front is spiking since ~11:36. Tail latency p95/p99 up ~3-4x. Starting correlation with infra logs.
netops-kim: I see transient packet loss on egress toward transit A (provider A) from our us-west-2 egress cluster. MTR shows 2-5% loss on a couple hops and sharp RTT increases around hop 6.
eng-runtime-maya: Any change in routing or recent deploys for gateway? Deploy-bot, did any rollout happen in the last hour?
deploy-bot: deploys: none to gw-usw2-front in last 2 hours. Canary to gw-usw2-r1 completed at 09:12 PDT.
sre-alex: Repro steps from support: curl -> gw endpoint returns 502 with body "upstream read timeout" and repeated auth token retries in logs. Sample curl:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","input":"hi"}'
```
Response headers show gateway timeout and backend connection resets.
netops-kim: I opened ticket with provider-noc — attaching MTR & traceroute. Provider acknowledges micro-congestion on peering fabric affecting ECMP across a subset of AS paths. They've flagged it as transit-saturation causing packet drops.
provider-noc: Confirmed. We see queue buildup at one of our aggregation POPs for ~11:30-11:50 PDT caused by a scheduled but rescheduled backbone maintenance on upstream. We're rerouting traffic now, ETA ~15-30m for stabilization.
cust-success-lina: Flagging impacted customers (acct ids 9872, 4421, 3309). They're getting a lot of retries and billing alerts. Should we pause rate-limited billing or mark usage as anomalous?
sre-alex: For immediate mitigation: 1) Shift gateway egress to alternate provider where available (policy-based routing). 2) Expand retry-backoff on SDK/edge for hosted API to reduce retry storm. 3) Add temporary rate limiting to heavy clients to keep backend healthy.
eng-runtime-maya: Can we flip a steering policy for the us-west-2 egress to prefer provider B for inference-only host routes? That should reduce packet loss exposure.
netops-kim: Initiating BGP community tag change for affected prefixes to prefer provider B. Will update once control-plane finishes announcing. Also enabling short-term path pinning to avoid flapping.
sre-alex: I pushed a config to increase gateway upstream timeouts from 30s -> 60s for this region to reduce 502s while transit stabilizes (will revert after). Logged rollout: `gw-config:timeout_usw2=60s`.
support-ryan: Noted — customers informed. Sharing suggested message to send:
"We're aware of timeouts/502s in us-west-2 caused by transit provider congestion. Our network team is rerouting traffic and applying mitigations. We're monitoring and will update in ~15 min. No data loss."
cust-success-lina: Sending now. Keeping customers on the loop and pausing billing triggers for the impacted tenant list.
provider-noc: Reroute complete for majority of AS paths. Packet loss should drop to <0.1% over next 5-10m. Continuing to monitor.
sre-alex: Observed backend error rate and gateway 502s falling; p99 latency back to baseline at 11:55 PDT. Marking as mitigated but keeping the incident open for postmortem and billing adjustments.
eng-runtime-maya: Please collect sample TCP dumps (pcap) from affected egress nodes and post them to the incident bucket for provider handoff.
netops-kim: PCAPs uploaded to s3://incidents-usw2/2598765432/pcap.zip. Filed support ticket with provider including those captures + BGP adj RIB snapshots.
sre-alex: Next steps: 1) postmortem with root cause (transit maintenance reschedule -> local queue saturation) 2) add routing preference escalation runbook 3) consider multi-provider HW diversity for critical egress clusters 4) adjust billing window for impacted customers. Assigning owners.
support-ryan: Thanks team — I'll keep the thread updated and close when postmortem links are up.
